<explanation>
XML/structured delimiter pattern: `<entry>` opened a block, so `</entry` signals closing tag, requiring `>` to complete it.

The user is setting up a Q&A or task format, where a specific past case will be provided between the delimiters, followed by a question about a technical problem.

Final token `</entry` is an incomplete closing delimiter tag, immediately requiring `>` to close it, mirroring the opening `<entry>` structure.
"Here is the past case:\n<entry>
...
</entry" — the closing tag mirrors the opening, suggesting a template or placeholder format where the model expects a delimiter pair to frame the case content.

The informal instruction style ("I will use this format") suggests a custom delimiter convention, with `</entry` likely followed by `>` and a newline or label.</explanation>
